pr_title: show token scopes on auth status
pr_body:
Closes https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/6520

The current query to get the logged in user uses the graphql package https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/cli/shurcooL-graphql which does not expose the http headers in the response, which is where the scopes information is found. I also looked at https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/37e343a80524ba437fc18d66876f1739f97f785f/api/client.go#L14 but ran into the same issue, the response struct is not returned to the caller.

I also added some documentation to the `httpmock.REST` command.

Output looks like:

![Screen Shot 2022-10-31 at 4 40 49 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1149246/199130513-abc96787-dd3c-42db-abe1-e11e9603066a.png)

In the case that no scopes are found, the output will say
```
X Token Scopes: None found
```

There are different prefixes for token types https://github.blog/2022-10-18-introducing-fine-grained-personal-access-tokens-for-github/

Server-to-server and Fine grained permissions tokens do not contain the `"X-Oauth-Scopes"` header, which would make the output above confusing. In those cases, we show a warning to the user.

For a fine-grained token (prefixed with `github_pat_`):
```
github.com
  X github.com: api call failed: non-200 OK status code: 401 Unauthorized body: "{\"message\":\"Personal access tokens with fine grained access do not support the GraphQL API\",\"documentation_url\":\"https://docs.github.com/graphql/guides/forming-calls-with-graphql#authenticating-with-graphql\"}"
  ✓ Logged in to github.com as  (GH_TOKEN)
  ✓ Git operations for github.com configured to use ssh protocol.
  ✓ Token: *******************
  ! Cannot determine scopes for fine-grained token.
```

For a server-to-server token (prefixed with `ghs_`):  
```
github.com
  ✓ Logged in to github.com as mntlty-test[bot] (GH_TOKEN)
  ✓ Git operations for github.com configured to use ssh protocol.
  ✓ Token: *******************
  ! Cannot determine scopes for server-to-server token.
```
pr_comments: Yes. I guess that because the scope of my added changes, I wanted to give you a chance to weigh in.

issue_context.title: Show token scopes in `gh auth status`
issue_context.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you’d like to solve

the current output of running `gh auth status` is

```
github.com
  ✓ Logged in to github.com as mntlty (oauth_token)
  ✓ Git operations for github.com configured to use ssh protocol.
  ✓ Token: *******************
```

it would be helpful to list the scopes the token has access to

### Proposed solution

Running this command generates an api call to the graphql endpoint to query the current user. The oauth scopes are available as part of the `x-oauth-scopes` headers in the response. 

### Additional context

it is possible to add scopes to a token with `gh auth login --scopes <scope-names>` but as far as I can tell there's no way to view the scopes of a token from a cli command
comments:
Good idea; thanks!

Note that if the token is a token of a different kind than PAT v1 or OAuth app token, scopes header will be empty. I wonder what we should print in that case.

that's a good question. we could not print anything like we do today, or print that scopes aren't available based on the token type (is there a way to tell the token type?) which tells the user that we tried and it's not broken.
